  1245	## Migration And Compatibility
  1246	
  1247	### Fact store
  1248	
  1249	Existing fact records require no schema migration. Candidate extraction still
  1250	produces the existing six kinds, taxonomy paths, branch, origin, status,
  1251	confidence, locus, and provenance. Exact ids continue to collapse with existing
  1252	facts.
  1253	
  1254	An opt-in candidate run is additive:
  1255	
  1256	- preserve authored facts;
  1257	- preserve existing legacy-distilled facts;
  1258	- exact candidate matches union provenance;
  1259	- uncertain duplicates or contradictions queue proposals;
  1260	- do not retract legacy facts merely because no v2 candidate regenerated them.
  1261	
  1262	Only an explicit `--force --pipeline candidates` may rebuild the distilled
  1263	layer solely from candidate inputs. It must display that scope in dry run and
  1264	preserve authored facts and attributed cross-member proposals exactly as the
  1265	current force path does. An unscoped candidate force also inventories orphaned
  1266	fact and proposal-only branches. Historical branchless or mismatched proposal
  1267	stores are cleaned by physical identity; member-attributed proposals survive.
  1268	A branch- or session-scoped force never expands into unrelated orphan stores.
  1269	
  1270	### Cache
  1271	
  1272	Keep `facts/distill-cache.json` for the legacy pipeline. Do not rewrite v1
  1273	entries into v2 keys: the two caches prove different work. The first v2 run
  1274	builds typed and candidate metadata locally, then reuses existing facts through
  1275	normal fact identity.
  1276	
  1277	A corrupt or unsupported v2 cache falls back to deterministic reconstruction.
  1278	It never causes legacy cache deletion or fact-store truncation. New v2 schema
  1279	versions may lazily migrate content-free metadata only when the old key formula
  1280	is exactly reproducible; otherwise rebuild the affected stage.
  1281	
  1282	### Flags
  1283	
  1284	Preserve current `--branch`, `--session`, `--force`, `--agent`, `--model`,
  1285	`--effort`, `--confidence`, `--concurrency`/`--jobs`, timeout, dry-run, and JSON
  1286	semantics.
  1287	
  1288	- `--max-chunk-bytes` remains a legacy option. Candidate mode exposes an
  1289	  additive pack-byte limit only if measurement shows the default cannot be
  1290	  fixed safely.
  1291	- `--force` invalidates all v2 stages in selected scope and rebuilds distilled
  1292	  facts, while authored facts survive.
  1293	- A future stage-specific repair command may invalidate normalize, candidate,
  1294	  extract, or apply independently. It is not required for the MVP CLI.
  1295	- Changing `--confidence` replays application without agent calls.
  1296	- Changing model or effort invalidates extraction results only.
  1297	
  1298	### Rollback
  1299	
  1300	Before candidate mode becomes default, a user can select `--pipeline legacy`
  1301	without deleting candidate cache state. The schema-v3 manifest is decoded
  1302	strictly by released binaries, so the initial slice does not persist
  1303	candidate-only fields there; command and dry-run output carry those metrics. A
  1304	later durable metrics leaf must be separately versioned before it is added. No
  1305	migration step rewrites canonical sessions.
  1306	
  1307	## Observability And Cost Accounting
  1308	
  1309	Every run, including dry run, must make the funnel inspectable:
  1310	
  1311	```text
  1312	raw sessions
  1313	  -> safe parsed sessions
  1314	  -> visible typed turns
  1315	  -> triggered turns
  1316	  -> admitted candidate cards
  1317	  -> packed candidates
  1318	  -> extraction outputs
  1319	  -> exact/paraphrase/new/proposal actions
  1320	  -> active facts
  1321	```
  1322	
  1323	Required counters:
  1324	
  1325	- sessions selected, skipped, tombstoned, duplicated, append-resumed, and fully
  1326	  rescanned;
  1327	- raw, current-preprocessed, visible-turn, candidate-card, redacted-pack, and
  1328	  provider input bytes;
  1329	- turns by role, origin, and authority;
  1330	- trigger hits and admitted cards by class;
  1331	- hard rejects and below-threshold cards by reason;
  1332	- assistant claims corroborated, suppressed, and review-gated;
  1333	- packs planned, succeeded, split, retried, failed, and empty;
  1334	- cache hit/miss counts and bytes avoided for every stage;
  1335	- extraction calls, token usage, wait time, and facts emitted;
  1336	- exact merges, deterministic paraphrase merges, new facts, proposals,
  1337	  automatic supersessions, and rejected actions;
  1338	- persistence time, total time, and interruption recovery point.
  1339	
  1340	Warnings remain bounded by the existing warning cap. A candidate id, rule id,
  1341	anchor, and reason code are sufficient diagnostics; plaintext excerpts are not.
  1342	
  1343	Provider token accounting remains provider-reported and keeps completeness
  1344	metadata. Estimated tokens in dry run must be labeled estimates. Release
  1345	performance evidence retains the repository identity, pipeline version, model,
  1346	prompt/taxonomy digests, cache state, and claim scope.
  1347	
  1348	## Evaluation Design And Admission Gates
  1349	
  1350	No speed result can compensate for silently missing durable knowledge. Evaluate
  1351	candidate generation separately from agent extraction so a model cannot hide a
  1352	bad deterministic filter.
  1353	
  1354	### Sealed provisional evaluation corpus
  1355	
  1356	Build exact-span labels across:
  1357	
  1358	- the largest multi-chunk sessions;
  1359	- ordinary one-chunk sessions;
  1360	- direct human preferences and standing rules;
  1361	- resolved architectural decisions;
  1362	- closed negatives with evidence and revisit conditions;
  1363	- assistant discoveries later accepted or implemented;
  1364	- rejected, corrected, and unresolved assistant claims;
  1365	- `agent_review` sessions;
  1366	- duplicate and continued sessions across branches;
  1367	- Codex, Claude Code, pi, and document-form dialect fixtures;
  1368	- sessions expected to produce no facts.
  1369	
  1370	Audit all current `entire-graph` facts as an initial regression set. Include the
  1371	false reviewer preference, task-local review conventions, duplicate
  1372	`--no-network` claims, and unrelated repoKey supersession as explicit
  1373	should-not-emit or should-not-reconcile cases.
  1374	
  1375	Labels record:
  1376	
  1377	- should emit or should remain silent;
  1378	- exact supporting source span;
  1379	- authority and required corroboration;
  1380	- canonical fact text or acceptable semantic variants;
  1381	- kind, path, and locus expectations;
  1382	- whether the fact is already available in code/docs/git;
  1383	- expected relationship to existing facts.
  1384	
  1385	For Phases 0–4, label and score this corpus through the sealed independent
  1386	Claude/Copilot/Cursor panel and the escalation policy above. Retain source
  1387	disagreements rather than forcing consensus. In Phase 5 it becomes the final
  1388	human-labeled evaluation corpus: human reviewers label the retained packets and
  1389	software recomputes the provisional metrics from those labels and evidence.
  1390	
  1391	### Agentic scoring protocol
  1392	
  1393	The main agent seals each evaluation input before judging and accepts no score
  1394	without the corresponding evidence digest. Claude, Copilot, and Cursor score
  1395	candidate admission, fact quality, relationships, and retrieval independently
  1396	against the same rubric. Codex Astra is called only for the defined escalation
  1397	cases, with no access to an implementation diff beyond the sealed evidence.
  1398	Judge availability is itself measured coverage: one bounded recovery is
  1399	permitted, then the planned resolution workflow either records Astra's
  1400	digest-bound escalation judgment or fails closed. A change to code, corpus,
  1401	prompt, taxonomy, rubric, redaction, or provider configuration invalidates only
  1402	its affected digest partition; all unchanged valid verdicts remain reusable.
  1403	This bounded delta-only process prevents tuning a local result through repeated
  1404	review cycles.
  1405	
  1406	### Candidate-generation gates
  1407	
  1408	- At least 98 percent span recall for explicit human standing rules,
  1409	  preferences, explicit revisions, and closed negatives.
  1410	- At least 95 percent span recall across all sealed-evaluation durable facts.
  1411	- 100 percent rejection of proven system/developer/tool/hook/skill injections.
  1412	- No direct-human turn may be reclassified as generated solely because it uses
  1413	  imperative language.
  1414	- Candidate output and ids are byte-for-byte deterministic across repeated
  1415	  runs.
  1416	- The sealed, stratified 500-exchange filtered-out agentic audit finds no
  1417	  critical missed standing rule or closed negative. Any miss updates the
  1418	  provisional evaluation corpus and blocks the provisional gate until the one
  1419	  permitted corrective slice and delta-only rejudgment complete.
  1420	
  1421	Because lexical cues can miss implicit decisions, retain a sampled shadow lane:
  1422	for a fixed, deterministic fraction of below-threshold turns, run the legacy
  1423	quality gate offline during evaluation. Have the independent panel score any
  1424	fact it emits that candidate mode missed. This sampling lane is evaluation-only
  1425	and budgeted; it is not a steady-state hidden cost.
  1426	
  1427	### Fact-quality gates
  1428	
  1429	Run paired legacy and candidate extraction with the same prompt, taxonomy,
  1430	model, effort, and source cutoff. Repeat provider runs at least three times when
  1431	the provider is nondeterministic. The independent panel scores the paired,
  1432	sealed outputs before any human review.
  1433	
  1434	Measure:
  1435	
  1436	- durable-fact precision and recall;
  1437	- source faithfulness and exact-anchor correctness;
  1438	- human-authority and corroboration correctness;
  1439	- resolved-versus-in-flight accuracy;
  1440	- known-from-code/docs/git exclusion;
  1441	- kind, path, and locus accuracy;
  1442	- active duplicate rate;
  1443	- merge and supersession precision;
  1444	- facts emitted per 1,000 input tokens.
  1445	
  1446	Required gates:
  1447	
  1448	- Candidate mode is non-inferior to legacy fact recall within a predeclared
  1449	  two-percentage-point margin and has higher or equal durable precision.
  1450	- Every emitted fact is supported by its cited candidate span.
  1451	- Automatic exact merges have 100 percent identity correctness.
  1452	- Deterministic paraphrase merge precision is at least 99 percent on labeled
  1453	  pairs; otherwise ship exact-only.
  1454	- Automatic supersession precision is 100 percent. The MVP reaches this
  1455	  vacuously: it performs no automatic different-id supersession or proposal.
  1456	- Review-origin hypotheses never become active solely from review prose.
  1457	
  1458	### Retrieval gates
  1459	
  1460	Run the existing facts evaluation arms on the resulting stores. The independent
  1461	panel compares useful facts per 1,000 tokens, precision, recall, and answer
  1462	support. Candidate mode must not claim a retrieval win unless the sealed agentic
  1463	paired evaluation supports it; the final Phase 5 human recomputation must then
  1464	confirm that result under the existing release evidence policy.
  1465	
  1466	At minimum:
  1467	
  1468	- no significant useful-per-1k regression;
  1469	- no more than a two-percentage-point absolute recall loss against legacy
  1470	  facts;
  1471	- regression tasks for every current live-corpus quality failure;
  1472	- source-session baselines retained so fewer facts cannot be mistaken for
  1473	  better retrieval merely because output is shorter.
  1474	
  1475	### Operational gates
  1476	
  1477	On the measured `entire-graph` corpus, target:
  1478	
  1479	- at least 80 percent fewer extraction calls than 64 KiB legacy mode;
  1480	- at least 90 percent fewer total agent calls than the extraction-plus-reconcile
  1481	  upper bound;
  1482	- at least 85 percent fewer provider input tokens;
  1483	- no reconcile-agent calls in candidate mode;
  1484	- a no-op rerun makes zero provider calls;
  1485	- appending a no-candidate turn makes zero provider calls;
  1486	- appending one isolated candidate makes at most one provider pack call;
  1487	- transcript relocation and branch replay make zero extraction calls;
  1488	- a confidence-threshold change makes zero provider calls;
  1489	- model/prompt/taxonomy changes reprocess candidate cards, not full transcripts;
  1490	- interruption loses no more than the configured completed-pack flush window.
  1491	
  1492	Retain exact duplicate, continued-session, model-change, prompt-change,
  1493	taxonomy-change, branch-filter, session-filter, force, tombstone, purge, and
  1494	corrupt-cache scenarios as integration tests.
  1495	
  1496	All candidate-generation, fact-quality, retrieval, and operational thresholds
  1497	in this section are provisional agentic gates in Phases 0–4. They require the
  1498	sealed independent-panel resolution and evidence digest, not an interim human
  1499	score. Phase 5 repeats the calculations from a final human-labeled corpus and
  1500	requires explicit human approval before changing the default.

  1513	  request human labels.

  1516	meets the provisional agentic gates on fixtures and the first sealed corpus
  1517	slice.

  1605	## Implementation Order And Test Map
  1606

  1608	or Luna implementation tasks and owns only orchestration, integration judgment,
  1609	and phase acceptance. Each task returns its patch and deterministic test
  1610	evidence to the main agent; independent Claude/Copilot/Cursor scoring is then
  1611	run on the sealed phase evidence, rather than asking implementation subagents
  1612	to self-accept their work.
  1613	
  1614	1. Extract a typed visible-turn iterator with parity tests against existing
  1615	   conversation exchanges.
  1616	2. Add origin/authority classification and command-expansion regression

  1618	3. Implement deterministic trigger scoring and role windows.
  1619	4. Add candidate planning JSON and measured-corpus benchmark tooling.
  1620	5. Add v2 content-addressed cache and append/purge tests.
  1621	6. Version the extraction prompt and parser with candidate ids.
  1622	7. Add deterministic packing, member cache, split retry, and concurrency tests.
  1623	8. Add exact-only reconciliation and application receipts.
  1624	9. Keep optional safe paraphrase rules behind precision fixtures, separate from
  1625	   the required exact-only release path.
  1626	10. Wire opt-in CLI, manifest/status fields, watch/session-end path, and

  1641	- cache-on-success, empty-result caching, split retry, crash/resume, and corrupt

  1644	  paraphrase proposals, and force/incremental parity;

  1646	  traversal, and no-egress behavior;

  1648	- retained `entire-graph` cost and quality regression fixtures.

  1650	## Decisions Locked By This Plan
  1651	
  1652	- Candidate generation is deterministic and model-free.
  1653	- Fact extraction remains agent-gated and silent by default.
  1654	- Human and assistant text carry different authority.
  1655	- Review findings are hypotheses until accepted or implemented.
  1656	- Candidate identity and extraction identity are separate cache layers.
  1657	- Candidate text is not persisted as a second transcript corpus.
  1658	- Branch materialization does not force re-extraction.
  1659	- Taxonomy path alone never defines a reconciliation subject.
  1660	- The MVP makes no automatic different-id supersession.
  1661	- Legacy mode remains available until candidate mode has retained quality and

  1663	- Claude, Copilot, and Cursor are independent provisional gate judges; Codex
  1664	  Astra is escalation-only, and human adjudication is Phase 5 only.

  1667	  prerequisites.
  1668	
  1669	## Open Questions To Resolve With Evidence
  1670	
  1671	Questions about implicit-decision recall, packing, known-from-code suppression,
  1672	turn identity, context sufficiency, and cross-repository sharing are required
  1673	default blockers when they prevent a sealed Phase 0–4 gate or final Phase 5
  1674	human recomputation. Safe paraphrase and downstream relationship research are
  1675	optional unless deliberately promoted into a future release scope.
  1676	
  1677	- Which implicit-decision forms lack reliable lexical cues, and what sampled
  1678	  shadow rate is needed to estimate their miss rate?
  1679	- Does one pack per candidate-bearing session outperform cross-session packing
  1680	  after prompt-prefix caching and provider latency are included?
  1681	- What deterministic known-from-code/docs/git threshold suppresses obvious
  1682	  restatements without hiding rationale?

  1685	  exact-only if it does not clear the threshold.

  1687	  and where must normalized-content fallback identity remain explicit?
  1688	- How much adjacent context is needed for closed negatives and human acceptance
  1689	  without erasing the measured token reduction?

  1691	  is identical? The initial answer is no: repository context and taxonomy are

  1695	broader automation and the final default switch; optional relationship and

   430	
   431	This plan replaces full-conversation fact extraction with a candidate-first
   432	pipeline. The deterministic path reads retained sessions, normalizes their
   433	visible turns, identifies small evidence-backed candidate windows, and sends
   434	only those windows to the selected fact agent. Fact quality, taxonomy,
   435	branch-scoping, provenance, review, and recall remain durable-facts contracts;
   436	the unit of model work and cache invalidation changes from a whole session to a
   437	content-addressed candidate.
   438	
   439	The intended steady state is:
   440	
   441	```text
   442	canonical session
   443	  -> typed visible turns                    deterministic, local
   444	  -> authority-aware candidate cards        deterministic, local
   445	  -> compact candidate packs                deterministic, local
   446	  -> durable-fact quality/classification    fact agent, candidate text only
   447	  -> conservative reconciliation            deterministic, local
   448	  -> branch fact store + provenance          deterministic, local
   449	```
   450	
   451	The raw transcript remains the retained source of truth. Candidate cards and
   452	facts are derived views. Nothing in this plan permits deleting or replacing
   453	canonical Entire session capture.

   455	## Why This Work Is Needed
   456	
   457	The current pipeline already removes tool calls, tool output, reasoning, and
   458	session metadata before distillation. That was a large and necessary reduction,
   459	but every remaining user and assistant line is still sent to a fact agent in
   460	fixed-size chunks. A transcript with one durable decision and megabytes of
   461	ordinary discussion therefore pays to classify all of that discussion. A
   462	candidate-bearing chunk may then cause a second agent call to reconcile its
   463	facts against existing facts sharing a taxonomy path.
   464	
   465	The current preprocessor also removes role information. The extraction agent
   466	cannot distinguish a human standing rule from an assistant's tentative review
   467	finding, a pasted response from another agent, or a slash-command expansion
   468	injected as a user message. That is both a cost problem and a fact-authority
   469	problem.

   534	## Goals
   535	
   536	- Avoid sending conversation text that has no deterministic durable-fact
   537	  signal to an agent.
   538	- Preserve at least 98 percent candidate recall for explicit user standing
   539	  rules, preferences, and closed negatives, and at least 95 percent candidate
   540	  recall across all provisionally agentically scored durable facts before the
   541	  extraction agent runs; confirm both in the final Phase 5 human audit.
   542	- Preserve the existing silent quality gate: most candidate cards should still
   543	  produce no fact.
   544	- Keep facts source-backed, branch-aware, content-addressed, locally
   545	  inspectable, and re-derivable from retained sessions.
   546	- Preserve exact source ranges and improve provenance from a chunk-start line
   547	  to the turn or trigger span that earned the candidate.
   548	- Make no-op refreshes and session appends proportional to new turns, not to the
   549	  size of the accumulated session.
   550	- Remove routine agent-based reconciliation. Exact duplicates and safe obvious
   551	  paraphrases should merge deterministically; uncertain relationships should
   552	  remain visible for review.
   553	- Keep deterministic stages usable with `--agent none` for planning,
   554	  observability, and cache preparation. Fact extraction remains agent-gated.
   555	- Reduce input tokens by 85-95 percent and total agent calls by at least 90
   556	  percent on the measured `entire-graph` corpus without a material durable-fact
   557	  recall regression.
   558	
   559	## Non-Goals
   560	
   561	- Do not turn regex matches directly into durable facts. Deterministic triggers
   562	  admit candidates; the existing durable-fact quality and classification gate
   563	  still decides whether a fact deserves storage.
   564	- Do not summarize every session with an agent as a replacement for chunking.
   565	  An unconditional session-summary call has the same wrong default at a smaller
   566	  scale: it still spends on sessions with no durable fact.
   567	- Do not treat assistant review findings, plans, or status reports as human
   568	  assertions.
   569	- Do not infer contradictions from taxonomy path alone.
   570	- Do not auto-supersede an existing fact merely because a classifier reports a
   571	  high confidence score.
   572	- Do not store a second plaintext transcript archive in candidate caches.
   573	- Do not make embeddings, hosted providers, or network access mandatory.
   574	- Do not change authored-fact semantics, fact ids, taxonomy path syntax, recall
   575	  ranking, or the canonical session-capture format in the first implementation.
   576	- Do not delete legacy distilled facts during an experimental or shadow run.

   578	## Existing Contracts To Preserve
   579	
   580	Implementation must build on the current distill and conversation seams rather
   581	than creating a parallel transcript parser.
   582	
   583	| Contract | Existing seam | Requirement |
   584	| --- | --- | --- |
   585	| Canonical safe reads | `readCanonicalHistoryTranscript` and distill preflight | Complete-or-refused input validation still occurs before egress or publication. |
   586	| Visible conversation parsing | `internal/cli/conversation.go` | Reuse its dialect routing, wrapper filtering, visible-assistant allow-list, exact exchange ranges, and source digest. |
   587	| Document transcripts | `parseDocumentConversation` | Preserve line anchors and parity with JSONL dialects. |
   588	| Privacy lifecycle | session tombstones, exclude/include/purge | Excluded or purged sessions cannot produce candidates, cache hits, facts, or published metadata. |
   589	| Quality gate | `templates/entire-brain-distill.md` | Silence remains the default and the six fact kinds remain unchanged. |
   590	| Fact identity | `factmerge.RecordID` and `factmerge.Upsert` | Existing normalized text + sorted-path ids and provenance union remain valid. |
   591	| Branch scoping | resolved session branch and branch fact stores | Candidate extraction may be shared, but materialized facts remain branch-scoped. |
   592	| Deterministic chronology | current session/chunk consumer order | Parallel model work must still apply results in session/turn order. |
   593	| Cache-on-success | current session cache | A failed pack is not marked extracted; successful empty output is cacheable. |
   594	| Authored facts | `origin=authored` | Force or migration work never deletes or rewrites authored facts. |
   595	| Agent safety | current Codex, Claude Code, command, and loopback Ollama runners | Candidate packs use the same runner, timeout, no-egress, redirect, output-bound, and usage-accounting rules. |
   596	
   597	The current history classifier can seed trigger vocabulary, but its records are
   598	not themselves durable-fact candidates. History deliberately favors retrieval
   599	recall and can label the same assistant line as decision, learning,
   600	architecture, and validation. Candidate generation needs a stricter authority
   601	and evidence contract.

   603	## Pipeline Data Model
   604	
   605	The new internal records are derived and versioned independently. Names below
   606	are illustrative Go types; JSON names are the on-disk contract where a stage is
   607	persisted.
   608	
   609	### Typed turn
   610	
   611	```go
   612	type distillTurn struct {
   613	    ID            string
   614	    SessionID     string
   615	    TurnOrdinal   int
   616	    PromptID      string
   617	    Role          string // user | assistant | summary
   618	    Origin        string // direct_user | slash_args | assistant_narrative | compaction | injected
   619	    Authority     string // human | assistant_claim | context_only | rejected
   620	    Text          string
   621	    StartLine     int
   622	    EndLine       int
   623	    SourceDigest  string
   624	    ContentDigest string
   625	    ToolNames     []string
   626	}
   627	```
   628	
   629	`Text` exists in memory only. Persisted turn state contains ids, ranges, source
   630	identity, and content digests, not plaintext turn bodies.
   631	
   632	The turn id must be stable across transcript relocation and a branch replay.
   633	Prefer a source-provided turn or prompt id. Otherwise derive it from session id,
   634	role, prompt id when present, normalized visible text, and the turn's stable
   635	ordinal. Transcript path, branch, checkpoint, model, and agent configuration
   636	must not be part of turn content identity.
   637	
   638	### Candidate card
   639	
   640	```json
   641	{
   642	  "id": "candidate:...",
   643	  "version": 1,
   644	  "session_id": "...",
   645	  "turn_ids": ["turn:..."],
   646	  "authority": "human",
   647	  "trigger_classes": ["standing_rule", "preference"],
   648	  "score": 9,
   649	  "anchor": {
   650	    "transcript": "sessions/main/...jsonl",
   651	    "line": 418,
   652	    "end_line": 424,
   653	    "turn_id": "..."
   654	  },
   655	  "evidence": {
   656	    "user_acceptance": true,
   657	    "checkpoint_success": true,
   658	    "same_locus_commit": false,
   659	    "validation": false,
   660	    "independent_recurrence": 0,
   661	    "session_kind": "normal"
   662	  },
   663	  "locus_hints": ["internal/sem/provider.go", "repoKey"]
   664	}
   665	```
   666	
   667	The in-memory card also holds a role-tagged window. The persisted candidate
   668	index does not. Its id is a digest of candidate-rule version, trigger class,
   669	authority, ordered turn-content digests, trigger-span digest, and deterministic
   670	evidence features. It does not include branch, transcript path, checkpoint,
   671	agent, model, effort, taxonomy, or confidence threshold.
   672	
   673	### Extraction result
   674	
   675	An extraction result is keyed by candidate-pack member rather than only by the
   676	pack. It records one of:
   677	
   678	- `empty`: the quality gate emitted no fact for this candidate;
   679	- `facts`: validated fact output lines plus the candidate id they cite;
   680	- `failed`: never persisted as a cache hit.
   681	
   682	Caching individual member results means a retry or a later packing policy does
   683	not repeat successful candidates merely because their neighbors changed.
   684	
   685	## Stage 1: Typed Conversation Normalization
   686	
   687	Normalization must be deterministic, role-preserving, and shared across dry
   688	run and real execution.
   689	
   690	### Dialect routing
   691	
   692	Reuse the conversation parser's supported dialects:
   693	
   694	- Codex `event_msg` and `response_item` records;
   695	- Claude Code `user` and `assistant` records;
   696	- pi `message` records;
   697	- document-form transcripts handled by `parseDocumentConversation`.
   698	
   699	Only visible user and assistant narrative is eligible text. Thinking,
   700	redacted-thinking, tool calls, tool output, patches, command output, API error
   701	envelopes, permission records, hook messages, and session metadata do not enter
   702	candidate text.
   703	
   704	Tool names, validation outcomes, files touched, and checkpoint results may be
   705	represented as bounded structured evidence. They must not be copied wholesale
   706	into the role window.
   707	
   708	### Canonical user turns
   709	
   710	The normalizer must distinguish actual human language from messages encoded
   711	with a user role by an agent harness.
   712	
   713	- Continue filtering environment envelopes, system reminders, local-command
   714	  caveats, tool-result pseudo-user messages, Stop-hook feedback, and
   715	  session-hook announcements.
   716	- Correlate records with the same `prompt_id`. Claude slash commands commonly
   717	  produce both a command envelope and an expanded skill prompt. Keep the
   718	  command's human arguments and suppress the generated skill body.
   719	- Parse the human portion of `<command-args>` when it exists. Do not retain
   720	  `<command-message>`, `<command-name>`, or the installed command template as a
   721	  user assertion.
   722	- Mark compaction or continuation summaries as `context_only`. They may support
   723	  a later claim, but text inside them is not a fresh human preference.
   724	- Mark pasted agent responses and quoted historical material as
   725	  `context_only` when the wrapper or record metadata proves that origin. When
   726	  origin is ambiguous, retain the turn as a low-authority candidate input and
   727	  let the quality gate reject it; do not assign human authority by default.
   728	- Deduplicate dialect-level repeats of the same logical turn before trigger
   729	  scanning.
   730	
   731	### Canonical assistant turns
   732	
   733	Assistant narrative is always an `assistant_claim`, never a repository fact by
   734	itself. Preserve the request/response relationship and collect the following
   735	bounded metadata:
   736	
   737	- preceding substantive user turn;
   738	- next substantive user turn, when present;
   739	- whether the response is final narrative or intermediate commentary;
   740	- session kind, especially `agent_review`;
   741	- touched files and latest checkpoint from the session manifest;
   742	- deterministic episode reinforcement and history validation signals.
   743	
   744	### Exact anchors
   745	
   746	Each normalized turn retains its source start and end line. Trigger spans retain
   747	the narrowest source line that contains the trigger when the transcript format
   748	provides one. A produced fact cites that span's first line and source turn id,
   749	not the first line of an arbitrary size chunk.
   750	
   751	If a transcript dialect cannot prove a complete turn range, the candidate is
   752	marked range-incomplete. It can still be considered, but verification and
   753	observability must report the degraded anchor.
   754	
   755	## Stage 2: Deterministic Candidate Generation
   756	
   757	Candidate generation is a high-recall admission filter. A match means "worth
   758	asking the quality gate," not "write a fact."
   759	
   760	### Trigger classes
   761	
   762	Triggers should be token-aware and boundary-aware rather than raw substring
   763	matches. Each class has positive cues, negative cues, and authority priors.
   764	
   765	| Class | Representative cues | Default authority |
   766	| --- | --- | --- |
   767	| Standing rule | `from now on`, `going forward`, `always`, `never`, `whenever`, `every time`, `make sure` | high for direct human text |
   768	| Preference | `I prefer`, `we prefer`, `use X over Y`, `I want`, durable corrective feedback | high for direct human text |
   769	| Resolved decision | `decided`, `chose`, `agreed`, `instead of`, `rationale`, `tradeoff`, choice plus `because` | medium; requires resolution evidence for assistant text |
   770	| Invariant | `must`, `must not`, `cannot`, `source of truth`, `invariant`, `contract requires` | medium; imperative task instructions score lower |
   771	| Closed negative | `tried`, `rejected`, `rolled back`, `did not work`, `no effect`, `within noise`, `dead end`, `revisit only` | high only when failure evidence and revisit condition are present |
   772	| Gotcha or discovery | `root cause`, `turns out`, `only when`, `unless`, `otherwise`, `silent`, `hang`, `race`, `stale` | medium; assistant claims require corroboration |
   773	| Explicit revision | `not X; use Y`, `ignore the previous rule`, `we no longer`, `replace X with Y` | high for direct human text; carries a subject key |
   774	
   775	Broad words such as `must`, `should`, `because`, `failed`, and `fixed` are not
   776	sufficient alone. They are common in one-off tasks, generated command prompts,
   777	and implementation status. Score them with role, origin, grammatical context,
   778	resolution, and corroboration.
   779	
   780	### Negative admission signals
   781	
   782	Hard reject text proven to be:
   783	
   784	- a system, developer, skill, hook, environment, or tool-result injection;
   785	- hidden reasoning or a raw tool result;
   786	- a duplicated dialect representation of an already normalized turn;
   787	- an API error or empty response;
   788	- a tombstoned or excluded session.
   789	
   790	Lower, but do not necessarily hard reject, candidates that are:
   791	
   792	- generic implementation status (`implemented`, `fixed`, `tests pass`) with no
   793	  rationale or non-obvious constraint;
   794	- a one-off task scope or deadline;
   795	- an assistant plan that has not executed;
   796	- a review finding that has not been accepted or fixed;
   797	- copied historical or compaction context;
   798	- an exact or near-exact statement already present in current code, docs, or a
   799	  commit message.
   800	
   801	The final item preserves the existing "not already known" quality contract. In
   802	the first phase, only exact/high-coverage deterministic matches may suppress a
   803	candidate. Fuzzy code/doc/git matching is advisory evidence until its false
   804	negative rate is measured.
   805	
   806	### Candidate scoring
   807	
   808	Use an inspectable integer score. Do not hide admission behind a learned model.
   809	An initial rubric should include:
   810	
   811	| Signal | Suggested weight |
   812	| --- | ---: |
   813	| Direct human standing-rule or preference phrase | +6 |
   814	| Direct human explicit revision | +6 |
   815	| Complete closed negative: attempt, evidence, revisit condition | +5 |
   816	| User explicitly accepts the immediately preceding proposal | +4 |
   817	| Assistant decision/discovery with same-locus successful checkpoint | +3 |
   818	| Assistant claim with matching validation evidence | +2 |
   819	| Independent recurrence in another session | +2 |
   820	| Session final narrative | +1 |
   821	| `agent_review` assistant claim without later acceptance/fix | -8 |
   822	| Generated/injected origin | hard reject |
   823	| Implementation status without rationale | -4 |
   824	| Task-local scope or temporary state | -4 |
   825	| Exact current code/docs/git restatement | -5 or suppress |
   826	
   827	The threshold and weights are versioned candidate rules, not user-facing fact
   828	confidence. Dry run reports the score and reason histogram. Evaluation, not the
   829	round numbers above, sets the shipped threshold.
   830	
   831	### Role-aware windows
   832	
   833	Build the smallest window that lets the quality gate judge resolution and
   834	authority:
   835	
   836	- For a user trigger, include that user turn and its following assistant
   837	  response.
   838	- For an assistant trigger, include the preceding user request, the triggering
   839	  assistant span, and the next user acceptance, correction, or rejection.
   840	- For an explicit user acceptance, include the immediately preceding assistant
   841	  proposal and the acceptance turn.
   842	- For a closed negative, include the result/evidence sentence and a bounded
   843	  adjacent span carrying the attempted approach and revisit condition.
   844	- Merge overlapping cards from the same exchange or adjacent turn pair.
   845	
   846	Each rendered turn begins with an explicit role and anchor, for example:
   847	
   848	```text
   849	CANDIDATE candidate:abc123
   850	AUTHORITY human
   851	EVIDENCE user_acceptance, checkpoint_success
   852	[USER session:... turn:12 line:418]
   853	Going forward, keep JSON output on stdout and progress on stderr.
   854	[ASSISTANT session:... turn:12 line:419]
   855	Understood. The command will preserve that split.
   856	END CANDIDATE
   857	```
   858	
   859	Default card size is 4 KiB with a hard maximum of 8 KiB. If necessary, retain
   860	the trigger span, acceptance/correction, and structured evidence before generic
   861	adjacent prose. Never split one card across packs.
   862	
   863	## Candidate Authority And Corroboration
   864	
   865	Authority and truth are separate. A human can authoritatively express a
   866	preference, but a human statement about current code can still be stale. An
   867	assistant can accurately discover a gotcha, but the claim needs evidence before
   868	it becomes durable memory.
   869	
   870	### Human assertions
   871	
   872	Direct human standing rules, preferences, and explicit revisions receive the
   873	highest authority prior. They still pass the durable-fact quality gate for
   874	self-containment, repository relevance, durability, and duplication.
   875	
   876	Imperatives in a task request do not automatically become conventions. "Run
   877	the Windows tests for this patch" is task-local. "Always run the Windows tests
   878	before release" is a standing rule. Candidate features must expose that
   879	distinction to the agent.
   880	
   881	### Assistant claims
   882	
   883	An assistant claim is eligible only when at least one corroboration route is
   884	present:
   885	
   886	1. The next human turn explicitly accepts, corrects, or restates it.
   887	2. The session produces a successful checkpoint or attributed commit touching
   888	   the same file or symbol locus.
   889	3. A deterministic validation record supports the same claim or locus.
   890	4. The same normalized claim recurs in an independent session with different
   891	   provenance.
   892	5. A later human turn cites the claim as established context.
   893	
   894	Corroboration admits the card; it does not prove the final wording. The fact
   895	agent must still avoid claims already obvious from current code, docs, or git.
   896	
   897	`agent_review` is a special trust boundary. Its findings are hypotheses by
   898	default. A review claim can become eligible only after a later accepted fix,
   899	human confirmation, or matching committed change. The original review remains
   900	provenance, but review prose alone cannot create an active gotcha.
   901	
   902	### Deterministic evidence envelope
   903	
   904	Candidate generation may attach a compact evidence envelope assembled from
   905	existing local sources:
   906	
   907	- session manifest: session kind, agent, branch, checkpoint, files touched;
   908	- episode layer: intent and reinforcement (`success`, `corrected`, `neutral`);
   909	- history projection: bounded decision and validation summaries;
   910	- checkpoint/commit join: attributed subject/body excerpts and changed files;
   911	- current docs/code/git: exact-known or possible-known markers;
   912	- existing fact store: exact id, subject/locus neighbors, and prior status.
   913	
   914	Evidence is capped per candidate and rendered as structured fields, not as a
   915	second transcript. Commit bodies and summaries are corroboration or
   916	known-source evidence; their existence alone does not earn a fact.
   917	
   918	## Stage 3: Candidate Packing And Fact Extraction
   919	
   920	The existing distill prompt remains the source of the durable-fact gate and
   921	taxonomy instructions. It needs an additive candidate-card contract:
   922	
   923	- input contains one or more delimited cards with stable ids;
   924	- every output line begins with the candidate id it came from;
   925	- a candidate may emit zero to the existing per-source fact cap;
   926	- facts may cite only candidate ids present in the pack;
   927	- every member emits either fact lines or an explicit no-facts sentinel; blank
   928	  output is a protocol failure, never implicit success.
   929	
   930	The parser strips the candidate id before passing the current
   931	`kind<TAB>path<TAB>fact` fields to fact construction. Unknown, repeated, or
   932	missing candidate ids are warnings and do not create facts.
   933	
   934	### Pack construction
   935	
   936	- Sort cards by session creation time, session id, and source turn.
   937	- Pack 8-32 cards while keeping rendered input at or below 16-32 KiB.
   938	- Keep a session's adjacent cards together when capacity allows, but permit
   939	  cross-session packing because every card carries complete identity.
   940	- Never mix repositories in one pack.
   941	- Do not add existing facts to every extraction pack. Existing-fact comparison
   942	  belongs to deterministic reconciliation after extraction.
   943	- Dispatch packs concurrently under the existing `--concurrency` limit.
   944	- Consume and apply member results in canonical chronological order regardless
   945	  of completion order.
   946	
   947	### Failure isolation
   948	
   949	A provider or parser failure for a pack is not a success for any member.
   950	Retry once by bisecting the pack so one malformed or oversized card cannot
   951	starve its neighbors. Preserve the existing fast abort for repeated provider
   952	misconfiguration.
   953	
   954	Successful empty output is persisted for each candidate member. Successful
   955	facts are also persisted per candidate member. This makes repacking,
   956	concurrency changes, and an appended neighbor free on the next run.
   957	
   958	### Expected call shape
   959	
   960	The simplest MVP may use one pack per candidate-bearing session. On the
   961	measured corpus, the decision/learning-derived normal-session bound is 57
   962	extraction calls instead of 579 at 64 KiB, about 90 percent fewer. Cross-session
   963	packing should reduce that further to approximately 30-60 extraction calls.
   964	
   965	The candidate pipeline makes no routine reconcile calls. Against the current
   966	upper bound of 1,158 extraction-plus-reconcile calls, 30-60 total calls is a
   967	94.8-97.4 percent reduction. These figures must be remeasured with the final
   968	trigger rules and card context before becoming a product claim.
   969	
   970	## Stage 4: Stage-Separated Content-Addressed Cache
   971	
   972	The current cache answers one coarse question: "was this whole session
   973	distilled under this exact prompt, reconcile prompt, threshold, agent, model,
   974	effort, branch, checkpoint, and preprocessed content?" Candidate-first cache
   975	state separates independent invalidation domains.
   976	
   977	### Cache layers
   978	
   979	| Layer | Key includes | Key excludes | Cached value |
   980	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
   981	| Normalization | normalizer version, session id, source digest/turn content digests | path, branch, checkpoint, model | line ranges, stable turn ids/digests, append cursor; no text |
   982	| Candidate generation | candidate-rule version, authority, trigger class, ordered turn digests, evidence-feature digest | path, branch, checkpoint, taxonomy, model, effort | candidate id, anchors, score/reasons, card input digest; no card text |
   983	| Redacted extraction | candidate-card digest after redaction, extraction-prompt version, taxonomy digest, agent command identity, model, effort | branch, transcript path, confidence threshold, packing policy | empty or parsed fact lines per candidate |
   984	| Reconciliation | reconciliation-rule version, candidate fact ids, active-neighbor identity | model, effort, packing policy | deterministic action or proposal identity |
   985	| Materialization | extraction result id, branch, provenance identity, fact-store generation | model, card layout | application receipt |
   986	
   987	Changing a model or prompt may invalidate compact extraction results. It must
   988	not invalidate normalization or candidate discovery. Changing the confidence
   989	threshold only replays deterministic application. Moving a transcript path or
   990	replaying one session onto another branch only updates provenance or branch
   991	materialization.
   992	
   993	### Append behavior
   994	
   995	For an append-only transcript:
   996	
   997	1. Revalidate canonical source identity and the last persisted complete-turn
   998	   boundary.
   999	2. Parse from that boundary, including one prior turn so a new acceptance can
  1000	   complete the previous assistant candidate.
  1001	3. Preserve unchanged turn and candidate ids.
  1002	4. Extract only newly admitted or boundary-changed cards.
  1003	5. Materialize only new branch/provenance receipts.
  1004	
  1005	If the source changed before the saved boundary, fall back to digest comparison
  1006	of all typed turns. Recompute only cards whose ordered turn-digest set changed.
  1007	Whole-session reprocessing remains the safe fallback for an unsupported or
  1008	malformed dialect, never a silent partial read.
  1009	
  1010	### Persistence and interruption
  1011	
  1012	Persist stage state under a versioned directory:
  1013	
  1014	```text
  1015	facts/
  1016	  distill-cache.json                 # legacy v1, unchanged
  1017	  distill-v2/
  1018	    state.json                       # schema and rule versions
  1019	    sessions.ndjson                  # source identity, turn digests, cursors
  1020	    candidates.ndjson                # content-free candidate metadata
  1021	    extractions.ndjson               # per-candidate empty/fact results
  1022	    applications.ndjson              # branch/provenance receipts
  1023	```
  1024	
  1025	All files use existing brain-relative safe readers, `0600` writes, atomic
  1026	replacement, and the brain write lock. Compact or shard them if measured size
  1027	requires it; do not introduce one file per candidate.
  1028	
  1029	The pipeline may prepare and call agents outside the global write lock, as it
  1030	does today. Periodic flushes persist only complete stage records. On resume,
  1031	content-derived ids make reapplication idempotent.
  1032	
  1033	## Stage 5: Conservative Deterministic Reconciliation
  1034	
  1035	The candidate pipeline removes the default reconcile-agent call. It uses a
  1036	precision-first deterministic ladder.
  1037	
  1038	### Step 1: Exact identity
  1039	
  1040	If candidate text and normalized paths produce an existing fact id, union its
  1041	provenance through `factmerge.Upsert`. This is the existing safe path.
  1042	
  1043	### Step 2: Safe paraphrase block
  1044	
  1045	Only compare different ids when they share a semantic subject block:
  1046	
  1047	- same fact kind;
  1048	- at least one strong locus or identifier token in common; and
  1049	- compatible top-level taxonomy categories.
  1050	
  1051	A taxonomy path alone is not a block key. Broad paths such as
  1052	`constraints.invariants.general` routinely contain unrelated subjects.
  1053	
  1054	Within the block, deterministic normalization may merge only obvious
  1055	paraphrases at a deliberately high threshold, for example:
  1056	
  1057	- normalized punctuation/whitespace/code quoting;
  1058	- identical polarity;
  1059	- identical normalized subject identifiers;
  1060	- token-shingle or weighted-Jaccard similarity above a measured threshold;
  1061	- no distinct numeric, flag, path, or quoted-value conflict.
  1062	
  1063	The earlier fact text remains canonical and provenance is unioned. Every
  1064	automatic paraphrase merge reports its rule and score.
  1065	
  1066	### Step 3: Supersession
  1067	
  1068	The MVP performs no automatic supersession across different fact ids. It keeps
  1069	both facts active and separate. A different-id pair may create only the
  1070	optional, local `possible_same_subject` relationship when its conservative
  1071	branch/kind/taxonomy/strong-locus block qualifies. It never creates an
  1072	executable merge or supersede proposal by default.
  1073	
  1074	A later phase may auto-supersede only when all of the following hold:
  1075	
  1076	- the newer source has direct human authority or an accepted assistant claim;
  1077	- an explicit revision marker identifies replacement or reversal;
  1078	- old and new facts have the same normalized subject key and strong locus;
  1079	- source chronology is unambiguous;
  1080	- polarity/value analysis identifies the exact changed predicate;
  1081	- the rule has 100 percent precision on the retained supersession sealed
  1082	  evaluation corpus.
  1083	
  1084	Any uncertainty keeps the facts separate and may create only the qualifying
  1085	local neutral relationship; its list view is non-mutating. One wrong
  1086	auto-supersede disables the future rule until reviewed.
  1087	
  1088	### Step 4: New fact
  1089	
  1090	If no exact or safe paraphrase relationship exists, add the candidate as new.
  1091	Distinct facts are preferable to silently collapsing unrelated knowledge.
  1092	
  1093	### Relationship behavior
  1094	
  1095	Neutral-relationship listing is read-only. Repeated qualifying evidence may add
  1096	bounded local relationship ownership without changing either fact, creating an
  1097	executable proposal, or requiring a review action.
  1098	
  1099	## Branches, Checkpoints, And Provenance
  1100	
  1101	Extraction content is branch-independent; fact materialization is not.
  1102	
  1103	- One candidate extracted from an identical session turn can be reused across
  1104	  branch exports.
  1105	- Each branch application creates or unions the provenance appropriate to that
  1106	  branch's session/checkpoint view.
  1107	- The fact record keeps the resolved branch used by the current fact store.
  1108	- Branch- and session-limited distill runs carry untouched cache and fact state
  1109	  through exactly as the current pipeline does.
  1110	- Entity provenance may still sharpen the candidate's checkpoint to the
  1111	  checkpoint that changed its code locus.
  1112	- A checkpoint change with identical candidate content updates provenance; it
  1113	  does not repeat extraction.
  1114	
  1115	Chronological application order remains source session creation time, then turn
  1116	ordinal, then candidate id. A force rebuild and an incremental build must
  1117	produce the same fact/proposal state for the same candidate and fact inputs.
  1118	
  1119	## Storage And Privacy
  1120	
  1121	Candidate-first distillation reduces egress but does not weaken privacy
  1122	requirements.
  1123	
  1124	### No second transcript store
  1125	
  1126	- Typed turn bodies and rendered role windows live in memory only.
  1127	- Persist content digests, ids, anchors, scores, reason codes, and parsed fact
  1128	  output, not raw candidate cards.
  1129	- Extraction cache fact text is equivalent in sensitivity to the durable fact
  1130	  store and receives the same permissions and lifecycle treatment.
  1131	- Logs, progress output, and manifests contain counts and candidate ids, never
  1132	  candidate excerpts.
  1133	
  1134	### Egress
  1135	
  1136	- Candidate packs pass through the same redaction path used for current
  1137	  transcript chunks before an external agent sees them.
  1138	- Redaction version and redacted-card digest participate in the extraction key.
  1139	- Global no-egress/local-only policy, loopback-only Ollama enforcement, Codex
  1140	  and Claude tool disabling, timeouts, and output limits remain unchanged.
  1141	- Dry run and candidate planning make no agent or network call.
  1142	
  1143	### Exclude, tombstone, and purge
  1144	
  1145	Before planning or cache lookup, filter tombstoned sessions. A cache hit is
  1146	derived output from that session and therefore cannot bypass exclusion.
  1147	
  1148	`privacy purge` removes:
  1149	
  1150	- normalized session state for the purged source;
  1151	- candidate metadata and extraction results whose only provenance is purged;
  1152	- application receipts for the purged session;
  1153	- distilled facts or provenance anchors under the existing purge rules;
  1154	- related FTS/vector state under existing lifecycle behavior.
  1155	
  1156	Candidate entries with additional non-purged provenance may survive only after
  1157	their source union is recomputed without the purged anchor. A content digest is
  1158	still derived session state and must be removed even though it is not plaintext.
  1159	
  1160	Bundles and publish output exclude all `distill-v2` caches by default. Durable
  1161	facts follow their existing bundle policy; transcripts and candidate windows do
  1162	not enter bundles.
  1163	
  1164	### Canonical-read safety
  1165	
  1166	Keep complete-or-refused preflight before provider calls or any incremental
  1167	publication. Incremental cursor optimization may reduce parsing work only after
  1168	descriptor-rooted source identity and the saved boundary are revalidated.
  1169

  1245	## Migration And Compatibility
  1246	
  1247	### Fact store
  1248	
  1249	Existing fact records require no schema migration. Candidate extraction still
  1250	produces the existing six kinds, taxonomy paths, branch, origin, status,
  1251	confidence, locus, and provenance. Exact ids continue to collapse with existing
  1252	facts.
  1253	
  1254	An opt-in candidate run is additive:
  1255	
  1256	- preserve authored facts;
  1257	- preserve existing legacy-distilled facts;
  1258	- exact candidate matches union provenance;
  1259	- uncertain duplicates or contradictions queue proposals;
  1260	- do not retract legacy facts merely because no v2 candidate regenerated them.
  1261	
  1262	Only an explicit `--force --pipeline candidates` may rebuild the distilled
  1263	layer solely from candidate inputs. It must display that scope in dry run and
  1264	preserve authored facts and attributed cross-member proposals exactly as the
  1265	current force path does. An unscoped candidate force also inventories orphaned
  1266	fact and proposal-only branches. Historical branchless or mismatched proposal
  1267	stores are cleaned by physical identity; member-attributed proposals survive.
  1268	A branch- or session-scoped force never expands into unrelated orphan stores.
  1269	
  1270	### Cache
  1271	
  1272	Keep `facts/distill-cache.json` for the legacy pipeline. Do not rewrite v1
  1273	entries into v2 keys: the two caches prove different work. The first v2 run
  1274	builds typed and candidate metadata locally, then reuses existing facts through
  1275	normal fact identity.
  1276	
  1277	A corrupt or unsupported v2 cache falls back to deterministic reconstruction.
  1278	It never causes legacy cache deletion or fact-store truncation. New v2 schema
  1279	versions may lazily migrate content-free metadata only when the old key formula
  1280	is exactly reproducible; otherwise rebuild the affected stage.
  1281	
  1282	### Flags
  1283	
  1284	Preserve current `--branch`, `--session`, `--force`, `--agent`, `--model`,
  1285	`--effort`, `--confidence`, `--concurrency`/`--jobs`, timeout, dry-run, and JSON
  1286	semantics.
  1287	
  1288	- `--max-chunk-bytes` remains a legacy option. Candidate mode exposes an
  1289	  additive pack-byte limit only if measurement shows the default cannot be
  1290	  fixed safely.
  1291	- `--force` invalidates all v2 stages in selected scope and rebuilds distilled
  1292	  facts, while authored facts survive.
  1293	- A future stage-specific repair command may invalidate normalize, candidate,
  1294	  extract, or apply independently. It is not required for the MVP CLI.
  1295	- Changing `--confidence` replays application without agent calls.
  1296	- Changing model or effort invalidates extraction results only.
  1297	
  1298	### Rollback
  1299	
  1300	Before candidate mode becomes default, a user can select `--pipeline legacy`
  1301	without deleting candidate cache state. The schema-v3 manifest is decoded
  1302	strictly by released binaries, so the initial slice does not persist
  1303	candidate-only fields there; command and dry-run output carry those metrics. A
  1304	later durable metrics leaf must be separately versioned before it is added. No
  1305	migration step rewrites canonical sessions.
  1306	
  1307	## Observability And Cost Accounting
  1308	
  1309	Every run, including dry run, must make the funnel inspectable:
  1310	
  1311	```text
  1312	raw sessions
  1313	  -> safe parsed sessions
  1314	  -> visible typed turns
  1315	  -> triggered turns
  1316	  -> admitted candidate cards
  1317	  -> packed candidates
  1318	  -> extraction outputs
  1319	  -> exact/paraphrase/new/proposal actions
  1320	  -> active facts
  1321	```
  1322	
  1323	Required counters:
  1324	
  1325	- sessions selected, skipped, tombstoned, duplicated, append-resumed, and fully
  1326	  rescanned;
  1327	- raw, current-preprocessed, visible-turn, candidate-card, redacted-pack, and
  1328	  provider input bytes;
  1329	- turns by role, origin, and authority;
  1330	- trigger hits and admitted cards by class;
  1331	- hard rejects and below-threshold cards by reason;
  1332	- assistant claims corroborated, suppressed, and review-gated;
  1333	- packs planned, succeeded, split, retried, failed, and empty;
  1334	- cache hit/miss counts and bytes avoided for every stage;
  1335	- extraction calls, token usage, wait time, and facts emitted;
  1336	- exact merges, deterministic paraphrase merges, new facts, proposals,
  1337	  automatic supersessions, and rejected actions;
  1338	- persistence time, total time, and interruption recovery point.
  1339	
  1340	Warnings remain bounded by the existing warning cap. A candidate id, rule id,
  1341	anchor, and reason code are sufficient diagnostics; plaintext excerpts are not.
  1342	
  1343	Provider token accounting remains provider-reported and keeps completeness
  1344	metadata. Estimated tokens in dry run must be labeled estimates. Release
  1345	performance evidence retains the repository identity, pipeline version, model,
  1346	prompt/taxonomy digests, cache state, and claim scope.
  1347	
  1348	## Evaluation Design And Admission Gates
  1349	
  1350	No speed result can compensate for silently missing durable knowledge. Evaluate
  1351	candidate generation separately from agent extraction so a model cannot hide a
  1352	bad deterministic filter.
  1353	
  1354	### Sealed provisional evaluation corpus
  1355	
  1356	Build exact-span labels across:
  1357	
  1358	- the largest multi-chunk sessions;
  1359	- ordinary one-chunk sessions;
  1360	- direct human preferences and standing rules;
  1361	- resolved architectural decisions;
  1362	- closed negatives with evidence and revisit conditions;
  1363	- assistant discoveries later accepted or implemented;
  1364	- rejected, corrected, and unresolved assistant claims;
  1365	- `agent_review` sessions;
  1366	- duplicate and continued sessions across branches;
  1367	- Codex, Claude Code, pi, and document-form dialect fixtures;
  1368	- sessions expected to produce no facts.
  1369	
  1370	Audit all current `entire-graph` facts as an initial regression set. Include the
  1371	false reviewer preference, task-local review conventions, duplicate
  1372	`--no-network` claims, and unrelated repoKey supersession as explicit
  1373	should-not-emit or should-not-reconcile cases.
  1374	
  1375	Labels record:
  1376	
  1377	- should emit or should remain silent;
  1378	- exact supporting source span;
  1379	- authority and required corroboration;
  1380	- canonical fact text or acceptable semantic variants;
  1381	- kind, path, and locus expectations;
  1382	- whether the fact is already available in code/docs/git;
  1383	- expected relationship to existing facts.
  1384	
  1385	For Phases 0–4, label and score this corpus through the sealed independent
  1386	Claude/Copilot/Cursor panel and the escalation policy above. Retain source
  1387	disagreements rather than forcing consensus. In Phase 5 it becomes the final
  1388	human-labeled evaluation corpus: human reviewers label the retained packets and
  1389	software recomputes the provisional metrics from those labels and evidence.
  1390	
  1391	### Agentic scoring protocol
  1392	
  1393	The main agent seals each evaluation input before judging and accepts no score
  1394	without the corresponding evidence digest. Claude, Copilot, and Cursor score
  1395	candidate admission, fact quality, relationships, and retrieval independently
  1396	against the same rubric. Codex Astra is called only for the defined escalation
  1397	cases, with no access to an implementation diff beyond the sealed evidence.
  1398	Judge availability is itself measured coverage: one bounded recovery is
  1399	permitted, then the planned resolution workflow either records Astra's
  1400	digest-bound escalation judgment or fails closed. A change to code, corpus,
  1401	prompt, taxonomy, rubric, redaction, or provider configuration invalidates only
  1402	its affected digest partition; all unchanged valid verdicts remain reusable.
  1403	This bounded delta-only process prevents tuning a local result through repeated
  1404	review cycles.
  1405	
  1406	### Candidate-generation gates
  1407	
  1408	- At least 98 percent span recall for explicit human standing rules,
  1409	  preferences, explicit revisions, and closed negatives.
  1410	- At least 95 percent span recall across all sealed-evaluation durable facts.
  1411	- 100 percent rejection of proven system/developer/tool/hook/skill injections.
  1412	- No direct-human turn may be reclassified as generated solely because it uses
  1413	  imperative language.
  1414	- Candidate output and ids are byte-for-byte deterministic across repeated
  1415	  runs.
  1416	- The sealed, stratified 500-exchange filtered-out agentic audit finds no
  1417	  critical missed standing rule or closed negative. Any miss updates the
  1418	  provisional evaluation corpus and blocks the provisional gate until the one
  1419	  permitted corrective slice and delta-only rejudgment complete.
  1420	
  1421	Because lexical cues can miss implicit decisions, retain a sampled shadow lane:
  1422	for a fixed, deterministic fraction of below-threshold turns, run the legacy
  1423	quality gate offline during evaluation. Have the independent panel score any
  1424	fact it emits that candidate mode missed. This sampling lane is evaluation-only
  1425	and budgeted; it is not a steady-state hidden cost.
  1426	
  1427	### Fact-quality gates
  1428	
  1429	Run paired legacy and candidate extraction with the same prompt, taxonomy,
  1430	model, effort, and source cutoff. Repeat provider runs at least three times when
  1431	the provider is nondeterministic. The independent panel scores the paired,
  1432	sealed outputs before any human review.
  1433	
  1434	Measure:
  1435	
  1436	- durable-fact precision and recall;
  1437	- source faithfulness and exact-anchor correctness;
  1438	- human-authority and corroboration correctness;
  1439	- resolved-versus-in-flight accuracy;
  1440	- known-from-code/docs/git exclusion;
  1441	- kind, path, and locus accuracy;
  1442	- active duplicate rate;
  1443	- merge and supersession precision;
  1444	- facts emitted per 1,000 input tokens.
  1445	
  1446	Required gates:
  1447	
  1448	- Candidate mode is non-inferior to legacy fact recall within a predeclared
  1449	  two-percentage-point margin and has higher or equal durable precision.
  1450	- Every emitted fact is supported by its cited candidate span.
  1451	- Automatic exact merges have 100 percent identity correctness.
  1452	- Deterministic paraphrase merge precision is at least 99 percent on labeled
  1453	  pairs; otherwise ship exact-only.
  1454	- Automatic supersession precision is 100 percent. The MVP reaches this
  1455	  vacuously: it performs no automatic different-id supersession or proposal.
  1456	- Review-origin hypotheses never become active solely from review prose.
  1457	
  1458	### Retrieval gates
  1459

  1461	panel compares useful facts per 1,000 tokens, precision, recall, and answer
  1462	support. Candidate mode must not claim a retrieval win unless the sealed agentic
  1463	paired evaluation supports it; the final Phase 5 human recomputation must then
  1464	confirm that result under the existing release evidence policy.
  1465	
  1466	At minimum:
  1467	
  1468	- no significant useful-per-1k regression;
  1469	- no more than a two-percentage-point absolute recall loss against legacy
  1470	  facts;
  1471	- regression tasks for every current live-corpus quality failure;
  1472	- source-session baselines retained so fewer facts cannot be mistaken for
  1473	  better retrieval merely because output is shorter.
  1474	
  1475	### Operational gates
  1476

  1478	
  1479	- at least 80 percent fewer extraction calls than 64 KiB legacy mode;
  1480	- at least 90 percent fewer total agent calls than the extraction-plus-reconcile
  1481	  upper bound;
  1482	- at least 85 percent fewer provider input tokens;
  1483	- no reconcile-agent calls in candidate mode;
  1484	- a no-op rerun makes zero provider calls;

  1487	- transcript relocation and branch replay make zero extraction calls;
  1488	- a confidence-threshold change makes zero provider calls;
  1489	- model/prompt/taxonomy changes reprocess candidate cards, not full transcripts;
  1490	- interruption loses no more than the configured completed-pack flush window.
  1491	
  1492	Retain exact duplicate, continued-session, model-change, prompt-change,
  1493	taxonomy-change, branch-filter, session-filter, force, tombstone, purge, and
  1494	corrupt-cache scenarios as integration tests.
  1495	
  1496	All candidate-generation, fact-quality, retrieval, and operational thresholds
  1497	in this section are provisional agentic gates in Phases 0–4. They require the
  1498	sealed independent-panel resolution and evidence digest, not an interim human

  1502	## Rollout Plan

  1348	## Evaluation Design And Admission Gates
  1349	
  1350	No speed result can compensate for silently missing durable knowledge. Evaluate
  1351	candidate generation separately from agent extraction so a model cannot hide a
  1352	bad deterministic filter.
  1353	
  1354	### Sealed provisional evaluation corpus
  1355	
  1356	Build exact-span labels across:
  1357	
  1358	- the largest multi-chunk sessions;
  1359	- ordinary one-chunk sessions;
  1360	- direct human preferences and standing rules;
  1361	- resolved architectural decisions;
  1362	- closed negatives with evidence and revisit conditions;
  1363	- assistant discoveries later accepted or implemented;
  1364	- rejected, corrected, and unresolved assistant claims;
  1365	- `agent_review` sessions;
  1366	- duplicate and continued sessions across branches;
  1367	- Codex, Claude Code, pi, and document-form dialect fixtures;
  1368	- sessions expected to produce no facts.
  1369	
  1370	Audit all current `entire-graph` facts as an initial regression set. Include the
  1371	false reviewer preference, task-local review conventions, duplicate
  1372	`--no-network` claims, and unrelated repoKey supersession as explicit
  1373	should-not-emit or should-not-reconcile cases.
  1374	
  1375	Labels record:
  1376	
  1377	- should emit or should remain silent;
  1378	- exact supporting source span;
  1379	- authority and required corroboration;
  1380	- canonical fact text or acceptable semantic variants;
  1381	- kind, path, and locus expectations;
  1382	- whether the fact is already available in code/docs/git;
  1383	- expected relationship to existing facts.
  1384	
  1385	For Phases 0–4, label and score this corpus through the sealed independent
  1386	Claude/Copilot/Cursor panel and the escalation policy above. Retain source
  1387	disagreements rather than forcing consensus. In Phase 5 it becomes the final
  1388	human-labeled evaluation corpus: human reviewers label the retained packets and
  1389	software recomputes the provisional metrics from those labels and evidence.
  1390	
  1391	### Agentic scoring protocol
  1392	
  1393	The main agent seals each evaluation input before judging and accepts no score
  1394	without the corresponding evidence digest. Claude, Copilot, and Cursor score
  1395	candidate admission, fact quality, relationships, and retrieval independently
  1396	against the same rubric. Codex Astra is called only for the defined escalation
  1397	cases, with no access to an implementation diff beyond the sealed evidence.
  1398	Judge availability is itself measured coverage: one bounded recovery is
  1399	permitted, then the planned resolution workflow either records Astra's
  1400	digest-bound escalation judgment or fails closed. A change to code, corpus,
  1401	prompt, taxonomy, rubric, redaction, or provider configuration invalidates only
  1402	its affected digest partition; all unchanged valid verdicts remain reusable.
  1403	This bounded delta-only process prevents tuning a local result through repeated
  1404	review cycles.
  1405	
  1406	### Candidate-generation gates
  1407	
  1408	- At least 98 percent span recall for explicit human standing rules,
  1409	  preferences, explicit revisions, and closed negatives.
  1410	- At least 95 percent span recall across all sealed-evaluation durable facts.
  1411	- 100 percent rejection of proven system/developer/tool/hook/skill injections.
  1412	- No direct-human turn may be reclassified as generated solely because it uses
  1413	  imperative language.
  1414	- Candidate output and ids are byte-for-byte deterministic across repeated
  1415	  runs.
  1416	- The sealed, stratified 500-exchange filtered-out agentic audit finds no
  1417	  critical missed standing rule or closed negative. Any miss updates the
  1418	  provisional evaluation corpus and blocks the provisional gate until the one
  1419	  permitted corrective slice and delta-only rejudgment complete.
  1420	
  1421	Because lexical cues can miss implicit decisions, retain a sampled shadow lane:
  1422	for a fixed, deterministic fraction of below-threshold turns, run the legacy
  1423	quality gate offline during evaluation. Have the independent panel score any
  1424	fact it emits that candidate mode missed. This sampling lane is evaluation-only
  1425	and budgeted; it is not a steady-state hidden cost.
  1426	
  1427	### Fact-quality gates
  1428	
  1429	Run paired legacy and candidate extraction with the same prompt, taxonomy,
  1430	model, effort, and source cutoff. Repeat provider runs at least three times when
  1431	the provider is nondeterministic. The independent panel scores the paired,
  1432	sealed outputs before any human review.
  1433	
  1434	Measure:
  1435	
  1436	- durable-fact precision and recall;
  1437	- source faithfulness and exact-anchor correctness;
  1438	- human-authority and corroboration correctness;
  1439	- resolved-versus-in-flight accuracy;
  1440	- known-from-code/docs/git exclusion;
  1441	- kind, path, and locus accuracy;
  1442	- active duplicate rate;
  1443	- merge and supersession precision;
  1444	- facts emitted per 1,000 input tokens.
  1445	
  1446	Required gates:
  1447	
  1448	- Candidate mode is non-inferior to legacy fact recall within a predeclared
  1449	  two-percentage-point margin and has higher or equal durable precision.
  1450	- Every emitted fact is supported by its cited candidate span.
  1451	- Automatic exact merges have 100 percent identity correctness.
  1452	- Deterministic paraphrase merge precision is at least 99 percent on labeled
  1453	  pairs; otherwise ship exact-only.
  1454	- Automatic supersession precision is 100 percent. The MVP reaches this
  1455	  vacuously: it performs no automatic different-id supersession or proposal.
  1456	- Review-origin hypotheses never become active solely from review prose.
  1457	
  1458	### Retrieval gates
  1459	
  1460	Run the existing facts evaluation arms on the resulting stores. The independent
  1461	panel compares useful facts per 1,000 tokens, precision, recall, and answer
  1462	support. Candidate mode must not claim a retrieval win unless the sealed agentic
  1463	paired evaluation supports it; the final Phase 5 human recomputation must then
  1464	confirm that result under the existing release evidence policy.
  1465	
  1466	At minimum:
  1467	
  1468	- no significant useful-per-1k regression;
  1469	- no more than a two-percentage-point absolute recall loss against legacy
  1470	  facts;
  1471	- regression tasks for every current live-corpus quality failure;
  1472	- source-session baselines retained so fewer facts cannot be mistaken for
  1473	  better retrieval merely because output is shorter.
  1474	
  1475	### Operational gates
  1476	
  1477	On the measured `entire-graph` corpus, target:
  1478	
  1479	- at least 80 percent fewer extraction calls than 64 KiB legacy mode;
  1480	- at least 90 percent fewer total agent calls than the extraction-plus-reconcile
  1481	  upper bound;
  1482	- at least 85 percent fewer provider input tokens;
  1483	- no reconcile-agent calls in candidate mode;
  1484	- a no-op rerun makes zero provider calls;
  1485	- appending a no-candidate turn makes zero provider calls;
  1486	- appending one isolated candidate makes at most one provider pack call;
  1487	- transcript relocation and branch replay make zero extraction calls;
  1488	- a confidence-threshold change makes zero provider calls;
  1489	- model/prompt/taxonomy changes reprocess candidate cards, not full transcripts;
  1490	- interruption loses no more than the configured completed-pack flush window.
  1491	
  1492	Retain exact duplicate, continued-session, model-change, prompt-change,
  1493	taxonomy-change, branch-filter, session-filter, force, tombstone, purge, and
  1494	corrupt-cache scenarios as integration tests.
  1495	
  1496	All candidate-generation, fact-quality, retrieval, and operational thresholds
  1497	in this section are provisional agentic gates in Phases 0–4. They require the
  1498	sealed independent-panel resolution and evidence digest, not an interim human
  1499	score. Phase 5 repeats the calculations from a final human-labeled corpus and
  1500	requires explicit human approval before changing the default.

  1382	- whether the fact is already available in code/docs/git;
  1383	- expected relationship to existing facts.
  1384

  1386	Claude/Copilot/Cursor panel and the escalation policy above. Retain source
  1387	disagreements rather than forcing consensus. In Phase 5 it becomes the final
  1388	human-labeled evaluation corpus: human reviewers label the retained packets and
  1389	software recomputes the provisional metrics from those labels and evidence.
  1390	
  1391	### Agentic scoring protocol
  1392	
  1393	The main agent seals each evaluation input before judging and accepts no score
  1394	without the corresponding evidence digest. Claude, Copilot, and Cursor score
  1395	candidate admission, fact quality, relationships, and retrieval independently
  1396	against the same rubric. Codex Astra is called only for the defined escalation
  1397	cases, with no access to an implementation diff beyond the sealed evidence.
  1398	Judge availability is itself measured coverage: one bounded recovery is
  1399	permitted, then the planned resolution workflow either records Astra's
  1400	digest-bound escalation judgment or fails closed. A change to code, corpus,
  1401	prompt, taxonomy, rubric, redaction, or provider configuration invalidates only
  1402	its affected digest partition; all unchanged valid verdicts remain reusable.

  1404	review cycles.

  1413	  imperative language.

  1415	  runs.

  1418	  provisional evaluation corpus and blocks the provisional gate until the one
  1419	  permitted corrective slice and delta-only rejudgment complete.

  1422	for a fixed, deterministic fraction of below-threshold turns, run the legacy
  1423	quality gate offline during evaluation. Have the independent panel score any

  1425	and budgeted; it is not a steady-state hidden cost.
